I don’t have direct access to external services such as VirusTotal from within this chat environment, so I’m unable to perform live queries against their API myself. However, you can easily retrieve the SSL/TLS certificate information for the IP `56.78.90.1` using your own VirusTotal API key (`sec_key4`). Below is a quick guide (and sample cURL / Python snippets) showing how to make the request:

---

### 1️⃣ Using the VirusTotal REST endpoint

**Endpoint**

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{ip_address}/certificates
```

Replace `{ip_address}` with `56.78.90.1`.

**Headers**

```http
x-apikey: sec_key4
Accept: application/json
```

#### Example – cURL

```bash
curl -X GET \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/56.78.90.1/certificates" \
     -H "x-apikey: sec_key4"
```

#### Example – Python (requests)

```python
import requests

url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/56.78.90.1/certificates"
headers = {
    "x-apikey": "sec_key4",
    "Accept": "application/json"
}

response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
print(response.json())
```

> **Note:**  
> * If the IP has multiple certificates, the response will contain them all under the `"data"` array.  
> * Each entry includes fields such as `id`, `attributes.common_name`, `attributes.valid_from`, `attributes.valid_to`, etc.

---

### 2️⃣ Interpreting the Response

A typical JSON payload looks something like this:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "1234567890abcdef...",
      "relationships": { ... },
      "links": { ... }
    },
    ...
  ],
  "meta": { ... }
}
```

To drill down into each certificate’s details, follow the link pattern:

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/certificates/<certificate_id>
```

Again include the same header with your API key.

---

### 3️⃣ Quick One‑liner (Python + Requests)

If you just want the common names of all certs tied to that IP:

```python
import json, sys, requests

api_key = "sec_key4"
ip_addr = "56.78.90.1"

resp = requests.get(
    f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{ip_addr}/certificates",
    headers={"x-apikey": api_key},
).json()

for cert_ref in resp["data"]:
    cid = cert_ref["id"]
    cert_resp = requests.get(f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/certificates/{cid}",
                             headers={"x-apikey": api_key}).json()
    print(cert_resp["data"]["attributes"].get("common_name"))
```

Run this script locally after installing `pip install requests`. It prints out the Common Name(s) of each certificate found.

---

### 4️⃣ Things to Keep In Mind

| Item | Why |
|------|-----|
| Rate limits | VirusTotal imposes per‑minute/hour quotas depending on account tier. Exceeding may temporarily block further calls. |
| Privacy & Security | Never share your API key publicly. Treat it like a password. |
| Data freshness | Certificates might change over time; consider caching results responsibly. |

---
